evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.21.94: quī mē imprūdente et invītō excidit, without my knowing (Lewis & Short: “not foreseeing … inconsiderate, imprudent”)
terms.comment: Its first sense is “not foreseeing, unaware”: imprūdēns does something without meaning or knowing it (see mean, intend).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 332.
